scope: Completed fixed-dimension phase only; reconstructed approximate windows, never exact inference markers.

method.nominal_decode_end: Remote JSON mtime, accepted only after remote/local SHA-256 and size match.
method.nominal_prefill_start: decode_start - JSON pp_seconds; omits the untimed prefill profile-write gap.
method.interior: Remove 1.0 second from each end. This is a sensitivity margin, not a measured confidence bound.
method.sample_selection: Include rows whose timestamp satisfies start <= t <= end; counts are samples, not time-weighted duty cycle.

code_order.benchmark: main.rs: prefill timer stops; prefill TSV is written; decode timer starts; decode timer stops; JSON println; final TSV is written; locals/Engine drop.
code_order.cleanup: Engine::drop waits for device idle and frees graph command buffers, queries, fences and semaphores before fields are destroyed. Wrapper completion follows subprocess exit.
code_order.clock_sampler: clockmon.sh timestamps before reading six sensors sequentially, truncates date output to milliseconds, then sleeps0.25s. Rows are neither simultaneous per-GPU observations nor utilization measurements.
code_order.mapping_note: Native Instance::amd sorts PCI bus order. The sampler comment about ggml Vulkan0 describes a separate reversed enumeration.

limitations: Nanosecond-valued filesystem mtimes are not nanosecond-accurate inference markers; serialization, stdout/filesystem behavior and timestamp granularity can shift anchors.
Remote/local content hashes match, and remote subsecond metadata improves copied whole-second anchors, but no exact monotonic-to-wall-clock alignment was instrumented.
The profile timestamps bracket phase transitions only approximately; sub-millisecond/few-millisecond agreement is an observed consistency check, not an error bound.
Clock rows timestamp before sequential reads and may miss brief clock changes; sample fractions do not establish continuous clock residency, elapsed-time duty cycle or GPU utilization.
The1s interior margin and shifted-anchor comparisons are sensitivity analyses, not a proof that every boundary error is within1s.
The clock log includes other work. Whole-command stats include loading/cleanup, and whole-log thermal maxima must not be assigned to these benchmarks.
No shader, build, model load or GPU workload was run for this analysis; only local reads and remote read-only file metadata/hash checks.

remote_metadata.operation: read-only stat and SHA-256 of 24 completed benchmark/profile/window files; no build, model or GPU access
